signs.label: Seizure / fit: shaking uncontrollably, paddling legs, not aware of you
signs.quote: seizures, trouble breathing, not responding to you or are unconscious

signs.label: Unconscious or not responding to you
signs.quote: Loss of consciousness

signs.label: Collapsed, cannot stand up, or suddenly very weak
signs.quote: Collapse should always be treated as a medical emergency.

signs.label: Trouble breathing: gasping, very fast or noisy breathing, breathing with mouth open (cats, rabbits, rodents, birds)
signs.quote: Trouble breathing

signs.label: Gums or tongue pale, white, grey or blue
signs.quote: Bluish or white gums or tongue
signs.note: Merck table column (immediate vs 24 h) was inferred from extracted text; VCA: "The presence of cyanosis means there is an emergency." (cats).

signs.label: Yellow gums, eyes or skin (jaundice)
signs.quote: a yellow tint may indicate jaundice
signs.note: Classified vet-now by us because, after a possible poisoning, jaundice suggests liver injury (xylitol, sago palm, paracetamol, mushrooms). No source explicitly ranks it as an emergency.

signs.label: Bleeding that will not stop, nosebleed, bleeding gums, big bruises, blood in urine
signs.quote: Excessive bleeding

signs.label: Bloody, black/tarry or uncontrollable diarrhea
signs.quote: Bloody, foul-smelling, or uncontrollable diarrhea

signs.label: Vomiting blood or "coffee grounds"
signs.quote: Vomit contains blood

signs.label: Vomiting again and again (more than twice), or vomiting plus diarrhea
signs.quote: Repeated or continuous vomiting or diarrhea, with or without blood

signs.label: Swollen, tight belly with trying to vomit but nothing comes up
signs.quote: Immediately seek veterinary care if your dog exhibits signs of bloat

signs.label: Cat straining in the litter box, passing little or no urine, crying while trying
signs.quote: A urethral obstruction is an absolute emergency, requiring immediate veterinary treatment.

signs.label: Cat has not eaten properly for 24 hours
signs.quote: If your cat has not eaten properly for 24 hours, seek immediate veterinary attention.

signs.label: Trembling, twitching, stumbling or walking as if drunk
signs.quote: Confusion, dilated or constricted pupils, ataxia (stumbling), tremors, seizures

signs.label: Racing or very slow heartbeat, extreme weakness or tiredness
signs.quote: Racing or slow heart rate, pale gums, weakness or lethargy, collapse

signs.label: Swollen face, tongue or throat; trouble swallowing
signs.quote: edema to the laryngeal region does not cause respiratory distress

signs.label: Bird fluffed up, sitting on the cage floor or low on the perch, not perching
signs.quote: not perching, sitting on bottom of cage for an extended period
signs.note: Same page: "Do not delay as serious illness can develop quickly."

signs.label: Bird breathing with tail bobbing, wheezing or open beak
signs.quote: A bird showing any of these signs should be seen by a veterinarian immediately.

signs.label: Rabbit not eating, or no droppings, for 12 hours or more
signs.quote: If your rabbit stops eating or producing feces for 12 hours or more
signs.note: House Rabbit Society: consider it an EMERGENCY. Merck: "Diarrhea or no droppings for more than 12 hours".

signs.label: Rabbit unusually quiet, hunched, not moving, not interested in food
signs.quote: needs emergency medical care is a loss of appetite and lethargy

signs.label: Guinea pig drooling or not eating
signs.quote: If your guinea pig drools or stops eating, see a vet quickly.

signs.label: Hamster, rat or mouse breathing hard, wheezing, or very lethargic
signs.quote: Breathing problems can become serious quickly in hamsters.
signs.note: Rats: Merck lists "lethargy, labored breathing" as reasons to see the vet.

signs.label: Hamster with wet fur around the tail, low energy, not eating
signs.quote: Signs include wet fur around the tail, low energy, poor appetite

signs.label: Vomited once and otherwise acting normally
signs.quote: Nausea, drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, or decreased appetite
signs.note: Outside a possible poisoning a single vomit can often be monitored (VCA); in this app the pet may have eaten something, so call the vet today.

signs.label: Mild diarrhea (no blood), otherwise acting normally
signs.quote: Nausea, drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, or decreased appetite

signs.label: Drooling, lip-licking, pawing at the mouth
signs.quote: Nausea, drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, or decreased appetite
signs.note: If drooling comes with mouth swelling or trouble swallowing → throat-swelling (vet-now).

signs.label: Eating less than usual but otherwise normal
signs.quote: Lack of appetite but no other signs of illness
signs.note: Merck table column inferred. For rabbits and guinea pigs, not eating is vet-now.

signs.label: A bit quieter or sleepier than usual
signs.quote: do not wait for the signs to worsen before getting help
signs.note: No source ranks "mild lethargy" precisely; cautious same-day call.

signs.label: No signs at all (yet)
signs.quote: Even if your pet is acting normal, contact your veterinarian or Pet Poison Helpline
signs.note: Many poisons have delayed signs (rat bait 3–7 days, lilies, xylitol liver injury, grapes, antifreeze).

rules.rule: Any sign of illness in a rabbit, rodent or bird → at least "vet-today"; listed vet-now signs stay vet-now.

evidence.quote: birds hide their sickness so they don't appear weak to other animals
Do not delay as serious illness can develop quickly.
Rabbits often hide illness, so quick veterinary care matters.
rodents do not show obvious signs of pain or disease until near death
Guinea pigs hide signs of illness until they are very sick.

rules.rule: Rabbits and rodents cannot vomit: "no vomiting" is never reassuring for them, and the app must never suggest making them vomit.

evidence.quote: the inability to vomit is a general property of Rodentia
Like other rodents, chinchillas cannot vomit.

rules.rule: Owner believes the pet ate something unknown but there are no signs → "vet-today" (call the vet or a poison line now; do not wait for signs). If the owner can see a likely culprit from the list below, switch to the identified-item path.

evidence.quote: Even if your pet is acting normal, contact your veterinarian or Pet Poison Helpline
do not wait for the signs to worsen before getting help

rules.rule: When several signs are ticked, use the most urgent verdict. Any vet-now sign overrides a dose-based "watch" or "vet-today" from toxins.json.

evidence.quote: Poisoning of any sort is an emergency.

rules.rule: Never give home-treatment instructions (no inducing vomiting, no salt, no hydrogen peroxide, no milk/oil). Bring the packaging or a photo of the item to the vet.

evidence.quote: Do not attempt to induce vomiting.

rules.note: Merck: salt as an emetic is "no longer recommended".
